newsitem.title: UK: Rank shares extend gains on buyback hopes.
newsitem.headline: Rank shares extend gains on buyback hopes.

text.p: Shares in British leisure company Rank Group Plc extended early gains on Thursday as the market breathed a sigh of relief at in-line results and looked forward to a possible buy-back at a later date.
Rank shares were 19p higher at 434p at 1150 GMT.
Rank earlier reported 1996 pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit of 297 million pounds, in the middle of market forecasts.
The possibility of a buy-back was raised after Rank said that it would ask shareholders at its AGM in April to authorise the company to purchase up to 10 percent of its shares.
Analysts said that Rank chief executive Andrew Teare had said that a buy-back was one option when the company looked at ways of improving shareholder value.
There was speculation that Rank might eventually use the proceeds of the sale of its remaining 20 percent stake in its Rank Xerox office equipment joint venture with America's Xerox Corp.
But analysts said Teare had told them at a briefing that there had been no talks on the issue so far.
Teare told the analysts that Rank would be setting a 15 percent return target from year two for future capital expenditure.
